blocks.text: 57 Morning Prayer for the New Year 57
ובכן
Therefore will we crown Thee.
יי מלך

The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,
The Lord will reign for ever and ever.
The mighty of the awe-inspiring people (Israel) swear allegiance aloud: The Lord is King.
uncertainties: The print breaks the word as 'alle-' / 'giance' across two lines. I joined it.

blocks.text: Those formed in lightning bless Thee aloud: The Lord has reigned.
The strong and lofty raise their voice aloud: The Lord will reign.

The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,
The Lord will reign for ever and ever.
The fiery in their haste utter aloud: The Lord is King.
The massed multitude praise aloud: The Lord has reigned.
And the hosts and the Hayoth testify aloud: The Lord will reign.

The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,
The Lord will reign for ever and ever.
Chanters of psalms sing aloud: The Lord is King.
uncertainties: The print breaks the word as 'a-' / 'loud'. I joined it.

blocks.text: The wise in mysteries confirm aloud: The Lord has reigned.
Princes in heaven glorify aloud: The Lord will reign.
uncertainties: The print breaks the word as 'a-' / 'loud'. I joined it.

blocks.text:
The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,
The Lord will reign for ever and ever.
Heirs of the precious teaching affirm aloud: The Lord is King.
The mighty in strength pay homage aloud: The Lord has reigned.
Those enveloped in flames give thanks aloud: The Lord will reign.
uncertainties: The 'd' in 'Lord' is damaged in the print and looks like 'Lor:d'. I read it as 'Lord'.

blocks.text:
The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,
The Lord will reign for ever and ever.
They who speak pleasing words say aloud: The Lord is King.
They who sparkle with brilliance triumph aloud: The Lord has reigned.
uncertainties: The print breaks the word as 'bril-' / 'liance'. I joined it.

notes: s142 has no rule line, so I read the whole page. The Hebrew page is set in two columns: the stanza lines on the right and the response (יי מלך / יי מלך / יי ימלך) on the left. I recorded each line in reading order: the stanza line, then its response.

Each stanza is a three-line alphabetical acrostic: א-ב-ג, ד-ה-ו, ז-ח-ט, י-כ-ל, then מ-נ. The rubric ע"ס א"ב משולש says this. The third line of each stanza is marked ק' (congregation). The first line has a siglum (ס' or ח') except in stanza 1, which has none. The rubrics say the ש"ץ chants and the congregation repeats.

Stanza 5 is incomplete on this page. Its third line (ס) and the refrain that follows are not here and presumably continue on the next scan. The English page s143 also ends after the second line of stanza 5.

The Hebrew on s142 is a piyyut with vowel points but no Biblical cantillation marks. I did not transcribe the small vertical strokes that may be meteg; I noted each one in the uncertainties for its line.

Overlaps between bands: band 2 repeats the end of the first refrain, band 3 repeats the טפסרי line, and band 4 repeats the נצצי line. I recorded each of these lines once, checked against the full page. On s143, the bands repeat 'The fiery…', the third refrain, and 'words say aloud…' / 'They who sparkle…'. I recorded each of those once as well.
On s143, the Hebrew cues ובכן and יי מלך are linkage only and are not part of the English prayer text. The English uses the same three-column layout and contains no rubrics or speaker sigla.

I found no clear source typos on these two pages. The hardest readings to settle are יְיַשִּׁירוּ (vs. יְיַשְּׁרוּ), וַחֲיָלִים (vs. וְחַיָּלִים) and נֹצֲצֵי (vs. נוֹצְצֵי). Please check them against the primary transcription; I am not proposing corrections.
